name: Indian Summer
approach: Western approach (the recommended option): roughly 10 miles with about 7,800 ft of gain via the Ptarmigan Traverse trail toward Spire Point — described as a 'brutal approach' with significant bushwhacking. A longer eastern approach via Chelan also exists but adds a full extra day each way.
overview: A 7-pitch, 5.10- granite rock climb up Dome Peak's South Face, established as a new route around September 2, 2011 — a rarely-repeated alternative to the standard Dome Glacier route for parties seeking real rock climbing on the peak.
beta: Seven granite pitches up the South Face, then scrambling to the summit. P3 has loose rock leading to an exposed belay beneath a crux roof and a leaning crack. P4-P5 are steep and solid on excellent granite, with P5 holding the technical crux, a steep stemming chimney. P6 makes a fine finishing flourish: a hand-crack leading to an arete and another hand-crack. P7 is short and completes the technical climbing; scramble from there to the summit.
fa: First ascent approximately September 2, 2011 (party included Nate Farr).
